title: Etale descent of codimension-one cycles and invariance of orders
statement:
Let $X$ be a regular Noetherian separated algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]: regular means all etale scheme charts are regular; Noetherian means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally Noetherian; separated means the diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is a closed immersion. For any such space or Noetherian etale scheme chart $Y$, let $\operatorname{Div}^1(Y)$ be the free abelian group on its integral closed subspaces of codimension one; codimension at a point is the dimension of a local ring on an etale scheme chart. For a quasi-compact etale map $v:Y\to Z$ between these spaces, define
$$v^*[T]=\sum_{T'}[T'],$$
where $T'$ runs through the irreducible components of $Y\times_Z T$, each with its reduced structure. This is a well-defined finite codimension-one cycle, and these pullbacks are compatible with composition. For every quasi-compact surjective etale scheme chart $q:U\to X$, writing $R=U\times_X U$ and $p_1,p_2:R\to U$, pullback is an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Div}^1(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{E\in\operatorname{Div}^1(U):p_1^*E=p_2^*E\}.$$

Local rings at codimension-one points of the regular scheme charts are discrete valuation rings. For an etale map $v:V\to U$ of Noetherian regular schemes, a codimension-one point $y\in V$ maps to a codimension-one point $x\in U$, and the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{U,x}\to\mathcal O_{V,y}$ takes a uniformizer to a uniformizer. Thus for every invertible meromorphic function $g$ on $U$ (a section of the units of the sheaf of total fractions described in [lem-sfb-space-meromorphic-generic-chart-model]),
$$v_y(v^*g)=v_x(g),$$
where $v_x,v_y$ are the normalized additive valuations, so the finite cycles of orders of such functions commute with etale pullback. The assertion applies as well to local meromorphic functions on open charts. No relative-dimension or equidimensionality hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

proof.text: For any space $Z$ in the statement, sobriety [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-sober] and unique reduced closed supports [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] identify integral closed subspaces with closures of individual points: an irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point, and its unique reduced closed structure is integral. Thus $\operatorname{Div}^1(Z)$ is the group of finitely supported integer coefficient functions on $Z^{(1)}=\{z:\delta_Z(z)=1\}$. The dimension used here is independent of the chart by [lem-sfb-space-local-dimension-chart-invariance]. This also applies to the closed subspaces below: closed subspaces of separated spaces are separated, as is seen by pulling back their diagonals to schemes, and closed subschemes of a Noetherian scheme chart are Noetherian, hence quasi-separated; quasi-compactness of the diagonal is all that the two cited point-topology lemmas need.

Here is the needed generic-point calculation. Let $T\subset Z$ be integral with generic point $t$, and let $a:W\to T$ be an etale scheme chart. By [lem-sfb-quasiseparated-space-etale-specializations], a generic point $w$ of $W$ maps to $t$: lift the specialization $t\leadsto a(w)$ to $w'\leadsto w$, forcing $w'=w$. Conversely if $a(w)=t$, every generization $w'$ of $w$ maps to $t$, and the same cited lemma forbids a nontrivial specialization in this fibre. Thus $w$ has no strict generization and is generic. More generally, for an etale map $h:P\to T$ of spaces with quasi-compact diagonal (closed subspaces of the separated spaces or of the Noetherian scheme charts of the statement), take a scheme chart $W\to P$. A lift $w$ of $p$ is generic if and only if $p$ is generic: one direction lifts generizations of $p$, the other uses the absence of nontrivial specializations in the fibre of $W\to P$. Apply the scheme calculation to the composite $W\to T$. Consequently the generic points of $P$ are precisely $h^{-1}(t)$. All these are statements about generizations and sobriety, so they also cover reducible $P$.

Apply step 2 to $P=Y\times_ZT$ for a quasi-compact etale $v:Y\to Z$. This fibre product is etale over $T$ by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. It is reduced: on scheme charts its maps to reduced charts of $T$ are etale, so [etale-proposition-etale-reduced] applies. Choose an affine surjective etale atlas $W\to Y$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. Since $Y$ is Noetherian, $W$ is locally Noetherian and affine, hence Noetherian. The inverse image $W_T$ is closed in $W$ by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], and has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components]. The closures of their images form a finite irreducible closed covering of $P$, hence $P$ has finitely many irreducible components. Their generic points are exactly the points $y$ over $t$ by step 2. A chart of $Y$ at $y$, composed with $v$, is a chart of $Z$ at $t$, so [lem-sfb-space-local-dimension-chart-invariance] gives $\delta_Y(y)=\delta_Z(t)$. Thus if $t$ has codimension one, all these components have codimension one in $Y$. Their reduced closed structures exist uniquely by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support].

proof.text: The displayed pullback therefore exists on each generator and extends additively to finite cycles. Write $c_E(z)$ for the coefficient of $\overline{\{z\}}_{\mathrm{red}}$ in $E$. Step 3 gives the explicit formula $c_{v^*E}(y)=c_E(v(y))$ for every $y\in Y^{(1)}$: different points of $Z^{(1)}$ have disjoint point fibres, and each generic component in a fibre occurs once. Its support is finite by step 3. For composable quasi-compact etale maps $w,v$, the coefficient at $y$ of $w^*v^*E$ is $c_E(v(w(y)))$, which is also the coefficient of $(v\circ w)^*E$. The identity has the same formula, proving functoriality without a dimension grading on components.

source.place: Tag 0EPY (lemma-etale-pullback); elementary coefficient calculation after steps 1–3.

proof.text: For the specified atlas $q:U\to X$, $R=U\times_XU$ is a scheme and its projections are surjective etale by [lem-a1-etale-atlas-presentation]. The map $q$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis, hence its scheme base changes $p_i$ are quasi-compact by the definition on scheme tests. The scheme $U$ is Noetherian: it is locally Noetherian as an etale chart of $X$, and quasi-compact because for the affine atlas $W\to X$ of [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas] the base change $U\times_XW\to W$ is quasi-compact, so $U\times_XW$ is quasi-compact and surjects onto $U$. Thus $R$ is quasi-compact over the Noetherian scheme $U$, and is locally Noetherian as an etale chart; it is Noetherian. Its regularity follows from its composite etale chart to $X$. By step 4 and $qp_1=qp_2$, every $q^*D$ satisfies the equalizer condition. Surjectivity of $q$ and chart invariance of dimension ensure each $x\in X^{(1)}$ has a point $u\in U^{(1)}$ over it. Step 4 recovers $c_D(x)$ at this $u$, proving injectivity.

Now let $E$ satisfy $p_1^*E=p_2^*E$. If $u,u'\in U^{(1)}$ map to the same $x$, [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] gives $r\in R$ projecting to both. Because $p_i$ are etale, chart invariance gives $\delta_R(r)=1$. Taking the coefficient at $r$ in the equalizer equality using step 4 yields $c_E(u)=c_E(u')$. Define $a_x$ to be this common value on each nonempty fibre over $x\in X^{(1)}$. The support of $a$ is contained in the image of the finite support of $E$, so is finite. Step 1 makes $D=\sum_xa_x[\overline{\{x\}}_{\mathrm{red}}]$ a cycle on $X$, and step 4 gives $q^*D=E$. Together with step 5 this proves the asserted isomorphism of abelian groups, including negative coefficients and the empty support.

proof.text: At any codimension-one point of a regular scheme, the stalk is a Noetherian regular local ring of dimension one by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. On a regular affine neighbourhood [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal] makes every local ring a normal domain; [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] therefore applies to give a discrete valuation ring. This argument works on arbitrary Noetherian regular schemes and does not require them to be separated or globally integral. For an etale map $v:V\to U$, a point $y$ and its image $x$, apply [lem-sfb-space-local-dimension-chart-invariance] to the identity chart of $U$ and the chart $v$ at $y$; the local dimensions agree. In particular a codimension-one $y$ has codimension-one image $x$.

Put $A=\mathcal O_{U,x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{V,y}$. Choose affine neighbourhoods $\operatorname{Spec}S\subset V$, $\operatorname{Spec}R_0\subset U$ with the first mapping to the second. Their restriction is etale (open restrictions and composition are covered by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]). By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the actual stalk map is $R_{0,\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-prime-generates-maximal], $\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}=\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$. Inverting $R_0\setminus\mathfrak p$ does not change the generated ideal, since its images are units. Hence $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$. If $t$ is a uniformizer of $A$, its image generates $\mathfrak m_B$ and is nonzero, since $B$ is a dimension-one DVR. It is therefore a uniformizer in precisely the sense of [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring].

For a nonzero $a\in A$, [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] writes $a=ut^m$ with $u\in A^*$ and $m\geq0$. The stalk homomorphism sends $u$ to a unit and $t$ to the nonzero uniformizer of step 8, so the image of $a$ is nonzero. Thus it extends to fraction fields. Applying the same factorization to numerator and denominator gives $g=ut^n$ for $n\in\mathbf Z$, and its image is $v^*(u)v^*(t)^n$. The normalized additive valuations on the DVR fraction fields are therefore both $n$. For the meromorphic function of the item these are its actual germs: [lem-sfb-space-meromorphic-generic-chart-model] identifies the chart restriction with the usual total-fraction sheaf and makes that identification commute with further etale restrictions. The calculation is local and so applies unchanged to functions specified only on an open chart.

proof.text: For completeness, the order cycles just used have finite support in the stated Noetherian situation. Regular affine rings are normal by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal], and their spectra have finitely many open-and-closed integral components by [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components]. We can consequently cover a Noetherian regular scheme by finitely many integral affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. On each, an invertible meromorphic function is a fraction $a_i/b_i$ with both entries nonzero, by the chart model [lem-sfb-space-meromorphic-generic-chart-model] (applied also to the separated affine chart itself). If its valuation at a height-one prime $\mathfrak p$ is nonzero, then $a_ib_i\in\mathfrak p$, since otherwise both are units in $(A_i)_{\mathfrak p}$. Such a $\mathfrak p$ is minimal over $(a_ib_i)$: an intermediate prime containing this nonzero element would be a nonzero prime strictly below a height-one prime, which is impossible. The closed subset $V(a_ib_i)$ has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], hence only finitely many such primes. The union over the finite cover is finite. The same proof works on open charts, which remain Noetherian. Finally the coefficient formula of step 4 and the equality of orders in step 9 give equality of the finite order cycles after pullback. Only local dimensions and finite support entered the proof; no equidimensionality or relative-dimension hypothesis was used.
